questions.question: February 2, 2019 will be Saturday. Then which day will be on October 4, 2019?
questions.solution:
Given that:-

Year 2019 is not a leap year so, there are 28 days in February.

So, February 2, 2019 will be a Saturday.

So, the number of days after 2nd February 2019 to 4th October 2019 are 26 + 31 + 30 + 31 + 30 + 31 + 31 + 30 + 4 = 244

Number of odd days in 244 days = 244/7 = 6

Thus, on 4th October 2019 the day will be Saturday + 6 days = Friday.

Hence, **"option 2"** is the correct answer.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Taj Mahal was commissioned in 1632 by the Mughal Emperor **Shah Jahan** to house the tomb of his favorite wife, Mumtaz Mahal.
 
• The construction of the Taj Mahal was completed in 1653, employing thousands of artisans and craftsmen.
 
• The Taj Mahal is located on the southern bank of the Yamuna River in the city of Agra, India.
 
• This architectural marvel is renowned for its stunning white marble dome and intricate inlay work with precious stones.
 
• The Taj Mahal is a UNESCO World Heritage Site and is often regarded as the pinnacle of Mughal architecture.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Mughal Architecture:**

 
 
• Mughal architecture is characterized by large bulbous domes, slender minarets at the corners, massive halls, and large vaulted gateways.
 
• It combines elements from Persian, Turkish, and Indian architectural styles.
 
• Examples include the Red Fort, Humayun's Tomb, and the Jama Masjid in Delhi.
 
 
 
• **Shah Jahan:**
 
 
• Shah Jahan was the fifth Mughal Emperor, reigning from 1628 to 1658.
 
• He is also known for commissioning other significant buildings such as the Red Fort in Delhi and the Jama Masjid.
 
• His reign is often considered the golden age of Mughal architecture.
 
 
 
• **UNESCO World Heritage Sites:**
 
 
• The Taj Mahal was designated as a UNESCO World Heritage Site in 1983.
 
• World Heritage Sites are landmarks or areas with legal protection by an international convention administered by UNESCO.
 
• They are recognized for having cultural, historical, scientific, or other forms of significance.

• It flows through several states including Uttarakhand, Himachal Pradesh, Haryana, Delhi, and Uttar Pradesh.

questions.question: What is Cash Reserve Ratio?

options.text: Percentage of deposits that a central bank must keep as cash reserves with the bank
Percentage of deposits that a central bank must keep as cash reserves with the government
Percentage of deposits that a bank must keep as cash reserves with any bank
Percentage of deposits that a bank must keep as cash reserves with the central bank

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Percentage of deposits that a bank must keep as cash reserves with the central bank**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Cash Reserve Ratio (CRR) is a crucial monetary policy tool used by central banks to control liquidity and inflation.
 
• Banks are mandated to keep a certain percentage of their deposits as cash reserves with the central bank.
 
• CRR ensures that banks do not run out of cash to meet the withdrawal demands of their customers.
 
• Higher CRR reduces the money available for banks to lend, thus controlling inflation, while a lower CRR increases the lending capacity of banks.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Statutory Liquidity Ratio (SLR)**

 
 
• Banks are required to maintain a certain percentage of their net demand and time liabilities (NDTL) in the form of liquid assets like cash, gold, or government securities.
 
• SLR is used by central banks to regulate the credit growth in the economy.
 
 
 
• **Monetary Policy**
 
 
• Monetary policy refers to the actions undertaken by a nation's central bank to control money supply and achieve macroeconomic goals such as controlling inflation, consumption, growth, and liquidity.
 
• Central banks use tools like CRR, SLR, repo rate, and reverse repo rate to implement monetary policy.
 
 
 
• **Repo Rate**
 
 
• The rate at which the central bank of a country lends money to commercial banks in the event of any shortfall of funds.
 
• It is used by monetary authorities to control inflation.
 
 
 
• **Reverse Repo Rate**
 
 
• The rate at which the central bank borrows money from commercial banks within the country.
 
• It is a monetary policy instrument which can be used to control the money supply in the country.

questions.question: National Rural Employment Guarantee Act was passed in which of the following years?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**2005**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The National Rural Employment Guarantee Act (NREGA) was passed by the Indian Parliament in **2005**.
 
• The act aims to enhance the livelihood security of households in rural areas by providing at least **100 days of guaranteed wage employment** in a financial year to every household whose adult members volunteer to do unskilled manual work.
 
• The act was later renamed as the **Mahatma Gandhi National Rural Employment Guarantee Act (MGNREGA)** in 2009.
 
• **Dr. Manmohan Singh** was the Prime Minister of India when NREGA was enacted.
 
• The scheme is considered one of the largest and most ambitious social security and public works programs in the world.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Objective of NREGA:**

 
 
• The primary objective is to enhance livelihood security in rural areas by providing at least 100 days of wage employment in a financial year.
 
• Secondary objectives include creating durable assets, improving water security, soil conservation, and higher land productivity.
 
 
 
• **Implementation:**
 
 
• Implemented by the Ministry of Rural Development, Government of India.
 
• The scheme operates on a decentralized, participatory planning approach.
 
 
 
• **Funding:**
 
 
• The central government bears the cost of wages for unskilled labor, 75% of the cost of materials, and certain administrative costs.
 
 
 
• **Transparency and Accountability:**
 
 
• Use of IT and biometric systems for transparency.
 
• Social audits and the establishment of grievance redressal mechanisms to ensure accountability.
 
 
 
• **Impact:**
 
 
• Has significantly contributed to poverty reduction in rural areas.
 
• Empowered rural women by providing employment opportunities.

questions.question: What is the retirement age of Judges serving at the Supreme Court of India?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**65 years**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The retirement age of Judges serving at the Supreme Court of India is **65 years**.
 
• This age limit is established to ensure a balance between experience and the need for fresh perspectives.
 
• Judges of the Supreme Court are appointed until they reach the age of 65, as per the Constitution of India.
 
• After retirement, former Supreme Court judges may be appointed to other judicial roles, such as in tribunals or commissions.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Constitutional Provisions:**

 
 
• Article 124 of the Indian Constitution deals with the establishment and constitution of the Supreme Court.
 
• Article 124(2) specifies that every Judge of the Supreme Court shall hold office until they attain the age of 65 years.
 
 
 
• **Appointment of Judges:**
 
 
• Supreme Court judges are appointed by the President of India.
 
• The Chief Justice of India is appointed based on seniority and consultation with other judges of the Supreme Court and High Courts.
 
 
 
• **Post-Retirement Roles:**
 
 
• Retired judges may be appointed to various commissions, tribunals, or as heads of inquiry committees.
 
• They may also serve as arbitrators in legal disputes.

• Kaal Baisakhi, also known as Nor'westers, is a local thunderstorm that occurs in the Indian state of **West Bengal**.

• **Formation:**
 
 
• Kaal Baisakhi is formed due to the heating of the land, which causes the air to rise and form cumulonimbus clouds, leading to thunderstorms.
 
 
 
• **Impact:**
 
 
• While these storms are beneficial for agriculture, they can also cause significant damage to property, infrastructure, and can lead to fatalities.

questions.question: Few renowned artists of ________ dance style in India are Roshan Kumari, Shovana Narayan, Maya Rao and Kumudini Lakhia.

__
 
• **Kathak:**

 
 
• Kathak is a major classical dance form originating from northern India.
 
• It is characterized by intricate footwork, rapid spins (chakkars), and expressive gestures.
 
• The word "Kathak" is derived from the Sanskrit word "katha," meaning "story," and story-telling is a key element of the dance.
 
• Roshan Kumari, Shovana Narayan, Maya Rao, and Kumudini Lakhia are indeed renowned exponents of Kathak, contributing significantly to its evolution and popularization.
 
• Kathak has strong Hindu and Muslim influences, and has evolved through both temple and court traditions.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

• Chhau is a semi-classical dance form with martial, tribal, and folk traditions.
 
• It originates from the eastern Indian states of Odisha, Jharkhand, and West Bengal.
 
• Chhau dances are characterized by vigorous movements, acrobatic leaps, and the use of masks in some styles.
 
• The dance often depicts episodes from epics like the Mahabharata and Ramayana, as well as local legends.
 
• There are three main styles of Chhau, named after the location where they are performed: Purulia Chhau, Seraikella Chhau, and Mayurbhanj Chhau.
 
 
 
• **Manipuri:**
 
 
• Manipuri is a classical dance form originating from the northeastern Indian state of Manipur.
 
• It is known for its graceful and fluid movements, particularly the raslila, which depicts the love story of Radha and Krishna.
 
• Manipuri dance uses distinctive cylindrical skirts (called 'kumil') and veils.
 
• The dance emphasizes gentle swaying movements and subtle hand gestures.
 
• The dance form is deeply rooted in the Vaishnavism tradition.
 
 
 
• **Odissi:**
 
 
• Odissi is a classical dance form originating from the eastern Indian state of Odisha.
 
• It is characterized by its tribhangi (three-bend) posture, graceful movements, and expressive facial expressions.
 
• Odissi dance is deeply rooted in the temple traditions of Odisha, and many of its movements are inspired by sculptures found in ancient temples.
 
• The dance involves expressions of divine and human love.
 
• Odissi was reconstructed in the mid 20th century, after a period of decline.

questions.question: A disease like COVID-19 is a kind of:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Zoonotic disease**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• COVID-19 is caused by the SARS-CoV-2 virus, which is believed to have originated in bats and potentially transmitted to humans through an intermediate host.
 
• Zoonotic diseases are infections that are transmitted from animals to humans. Examples include Ebola, Rabies, and Avian Influenza.
 
• Such diseases can spread through direct contact with animals, by consuming contaminated food or water, or via vectors like mosquitoes.
 
• Zoonotic diseases pose significant challenges to public health due to their potential for widespread outbreaks and pandemics.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Terminology:**

 
 
• **Zoonosis:** An infectious disease that has jumped from a non-human animal to humans.
 
• **Vector:** An organism, typically a biting insect or tick, that transmits a disease or parasite from one animal or plant to another.
 
 
 
• **Examples of Zoonotic Diseases:**
 
 
• **Ebola:** Transmitted to humans through contact with blood, secretions, organs, or other bodily fluids of infected animals.
 
• **Rabies:** A viral disease that causes inflammation of the brain in humans and other mammals.
 
• **Avian Influenza:** Commonly known as bird flu, it is a viral infection that can infect not only birds but also humans and other animals.
 
 
 
• **COVID-19 Transmission:**
 
 
• The primary mode of transmission is through respiratory droplets when an infected person coughs, sneezes, or talks.
 
• It can also spread by touching surfaces contaminated with the virus and then touching the face.
 
 
 
• **Public Health Measures:**
 
 
• Preventive measures include wearing masks, practicing hand hygiene, and maintaining physical distance.
 
• Controlling zoonotic diseases involves monitoring animal health, regulating wildlife trade, and ensuring food safety.

**Given:**

Width of the rectangle = 195 cm

The diagonal of the rectangle = 507 cm

**Formula Used:**

Let the length of the rectangle be "l".

According to the Pythagorean theorem, for any right-angled triangle, the sum of the squares of the two shorter sides equals the square of the hypotenuse (the longest side). In this case, we can use this formula to find the length of the rectangle, as follows:

l² = d² - w²

where d is the diagonal length, w is the rectangle's width.

**Solution:**

We know that the width of the rectangle is 195 cm.

Let the length of the rectangle be "l".

Using the Pythagorean theorem, we have:

l2 = d2 - w2

Substituting the given values, we get:

l2 = (507 cm)² - (195 cm)²

l2 = (507 +195)(507 - 195)

l2 = (702)(312)

l2 = 219024

Taking the square root of both sides, we get:

l = √(219024) cm

l = 468

**Therefore, the length of the rectangle is 468 cm, and its width is 195 cm.**
